notes: Clicked for credits for six-plus turns while sitting on 20-37 credits and never contested the advanced remotes; later re-ran HQ over and over seeing the same Mindscaping/Tatu-Bola while the Corp scored, and on the last turn drew instead of running the freshly installed remote that won the game.

Sat on 20-28 credits with very little ice and installed Tomorrow's Headline, False Lead and Project Beale behind a single weak ice each, all stolen; the tag/meat-damage plan eventually flatlined the Runner.

Spent all money on Carmen turn 1 and lived at 0 credits for the rest of the game, repeatedly running into Bellona and Degree Mill it could not afford to steal and re-running HQ to see the same cards while the Corp advanced and scored from Server 10.

Turn-1 Above the Law behind one ice was stolen; afterwards the Corp played safely with iced remotes but took 22 turns against a Runner that almost never ran, spending many turns advancing ice and drawing instead of pressing agendas.

Reasonable early R&D/HQ pressure (Degree Mill, False Lead), but left a tag up for End of the Line, ran a three-ice remote with no breakers into Tsarevna and then lost the hand to Orbital Superiority, and spent many mid-game clicks clicking for credits with a full grip.

Clicked for credits for four straight turns while discarding cards, left R&D open and HQ behind a lone Ping while holding Bellonas and False Lead, and never installed or scored anything before losing on turn 7; the four-tag Oppo Research was never followed up.
Slow setup with some idle credit clicks and frequent Archives checks, but built a sensible Botulus/Audrey rig, handled Anemone, and converted HQ pressure into a turn-13 win.

Clicked for credits for ten turns up to 46 credits without running while the Corp scored two Regenesis, then ran a known Anansi with three cards in grip and stole House of Knives into a foreseeable flatline.

Never installed an agenda in 23 turns, clicking for credits to 30 while discarding every turn and leaving agendas in an HQ guarded only by Ping; shuffled agendas away with Attitude Adjustment and wasted late turns repeatedly trashing resources instead of scoring or killing a broke, tagged Runner.
Early Send a Message score was good and remotes were well iced, but the middle game was a dozen turns of hoarding 20-36 credits and advancing ice without installing agendas against a passive Runner.
Left R&D completely unprotected and lost Fujii to it, but scored See How They Run and followed with End of the Line for a clean turn-4 flatline.

Early play was fine (stole Project Beale, trashed Regolith), but the late game was spent clicking for credits up to 50 with one card in grip while the Corp scored False Lead and two Degree Mills from a single remote unchallenged.
Clicked for credits for 13 turns up to 45 credits with R&D unprotected and discarded Tomorrow's Headline to an open Archives; it eventually built one remote and won, but the opening was a long pause.

Sat at 0 credits from turn 3 on, spending every click re-running R&D (often seeing the same top card) and never gaining money, removing tags or playing its hand, then got flatlined by End of the Line while heavily tagged.

Built a steady economy and used Boomerang/Aumakua to keep R&D and Archives pressure on, stealing three agendas for a turn-19 win; some idle Archives runs and couldn't stop SDS from the heavily iced remote.
Took credits on turn 1 with no HQ ice while holding agendas, losing three to an open HQ by turn 2, then clicked for credits and discarded for many turns, losing the last agenda from Archives.
Never ran the single remote while the Corp, often at 0-4 credits, advanced and scored three agendas back to back; the Runner just clicked for credits, drew, and checked Archives.
Coherent PE plan with a punishing Vampyronassa on R&D and steady remote scoring; minor issues were early credit clicks while discarding and a Sting! lost behind unrezzable ice.
The Bladderwort net-damage engine won by turn-7 flatline, but the Corp stayed at 0-3 credits and advanced Fujii behind ice it could not afford to rez, giving away 3 points.
Hammering an unprotected R&D won on turn 5, but the Runner sat at 0 credits all game and spent many clicks re-running R&D to see the same top card instead of gaining money or checking the remotes.
